app.title: Lamplight Nook
app.tagline: A cozy pixel shop where a small team does computer jobs for you with Claude.

risk.secretFile: "{name}" looks like a file with secrets in it
risk.hiddenConfig: this is hidden settings for programs on your computer
risk.outsideFolder: it writes outside the commission folder
risk.overwrite: it overwrites "{name}", which was there before
risk.delegate: sends a helper to do something
risk.noTarget: it isn't clear where it would write
risk.write: writes a file in the commission folder
risk.delete: deletes or moves files, and that can't be undone
risk.repairGit: branches and commits are the shop's job; the fixer only looks with git
risk.repairTests: runs the repository's tests, which run its own code
risk.complexCommand: this command is complicated and I can't be sure what it does
risk.inlineCode: runs code written on the spot; I can't tell what it will do
risk.readOutside: reads something outside the commission folder
risk.shellAfterConnection: This commission has read from "{label}", so it asks you before running a command
risk.webAfterConnection: This commission has read from "{label}", so it asks you before going online
risk.connectionsPaused: All connections are paused in settings
risk.safeCommand: runs a read-only command in the commission folder
risk.unknownCommand: wants to run "{name}" and I can't be sure what it does
risk.unknownTool: wants to use a tool I don't know, "{tool}"

nook.make: only makes new files in this commission's folder
nook.outside: changes something outside this commission's folder, which can be undone

handin.firstToggle: The counter opens the hand-in first, not the slip
handin.firstHint: No typing: drag materials over, pick a sample, click Wick's answers, then sign. The slip is still there, one click away on the card.

repair.tallyNothing: The fixer is looking through the repository
repair.testsNotSeen: The shop didn't see the tests run, so run them once yourself.
repair.say: It's fixed, and here's the review sheet. Approve it and the branch stays; merging is up to you.
repair.kept: The branch {branch} is in your repository. Merging it is up to you.
repair.dropped: The branch is deleted. Your repository is as it was when you lent it.

layout.label: Layout:
layout.journalHint: One A4 page, portrait: the route, a list for each day and a small map of the route drawn on it. Saved as a PDF to print and take along.

templates.label: Pick one, or just write
templates.pageFill: Make me a small web page that ...
templates.researchFill: Look into ... and write me a short summary.
templates.tidyFill: How should I tidy up this folder? ...
templates.albumFill: Make a little album of these photos: ...
templates.travelFill: Make me a travel guide for ..., ... days.
templates.toolFill: Make me a small tool that ...
templates.documentFill: Write me a Word document about ...
templates.slidesFill: Make me slides about ..., about ... slides.
templates.chartFill: Draw a chart of ... from these numbers: ...
templates.posterFill: Make a poster for ..., on ... at ...
templates.chartHint: Write the numbers in the request, or hand over the table (Excel or CSV). Every number on the chart is copied from yours; you get a picture and the page it was drawn from.
templates.posterHint: Say what it is for: printing (A4), a social post (square) or a screen (wide). Hand over photos to put on it if you like. Missing dates or places are left blank for you.
templates.menuFill: Make a menu for ..., with these dishes: ...
templates.menuHint: Write the dishes and prices in the request, or hand over an old menu or a table. Dishes and prices are copied exactly; anything missing is left blank for you. Say what it is for: printing (A4), a social post (square) or a screen in the shop (wide).
templates.recipeFill: Write up ... as a recipe, for ... people.
templates.recipeHint: Write down the dish and how you usually make it, or hand over a photo of a handwritten card. Where you give no amounts, everyday ones are used, marked as a starting point to adjust.
templates.cardHint: Say what the day is and who it is for, and write what you want it to say in the request. Hand over a photo to put on it if you like. You get a picture, and a PDF to print.
templates.newsletterFill: Make a newsletter for ..., this issue about: ...
templates.newsletterHint: Write what this issue covers in the request, or hand over notes and photos. Only what you give goes in; missing dates and names are left blank for you. You get a Word document and a PDF.
templates.flashcardsFill: Turn this ... into revision cards, for a test on: ...
templates.flashcardsHint: Hand over a handout, notes or a chapter, or paste it into the request. Every question and answer comes from it alone: cards to print and cut apart, and a ten-question quiz with the answers on the back.
templates.ledgerbookFill: Make me a family ledger, starting from ..., where our money mostly goes on: ...
templates.minigameFill: Make me a small game for ... to play, something like ...
templates.minigameHint: The workshop makes a small game to play in a browser: one file that opens and plays with no network. Say who will play and what kind of game, such as matching pairs, whack-a-mole or snake.
templates.comicFill: Draw me a four-panel comic about ..., with the lines: ...
templates.comicHint: The studio draws a four-panel comic strip: four panels top to bottom, the lines in speech bubbles. Your own lines are used as written; if you give none, Iris writes them. You get one long picture and a PDF.
templates.picturebookFill: Make a bedtime picture book for ..., who loves ...
templates.picturebookHint: The studio draws a bedtime picture book of about eight pages, a picture and a short passage on each, and the print shop lays it out as a landscape PDF. The cover has the title and the child's name. Give an opening to the story, or just the child's name and what they love.
templates.ledgerbookHint: The print shop makes an Excel ledger: a sheet a month, and the categories for money in and out on a sheet of their own, to change any time. The month's summary and pie chart work themselves out, so the empty book is ready to fill in.
templates.resumeHint: Hand over an old résumé or a list of what you've done, if you have one. Nothing gets made up; gaps are left for you to fill in.
templates.notesHint: Hand over your highlights and jottings. Quotations come only from what you hand over.
templates.toolHint: If it can work in a browser, it becomes a web page. A script only when files on your computer must change, and it only lists what it would do until you run it with -Apply.
templates.albumHint: Hand over the photos: drag them onto this slip, or use "Hand over files". The album is a web page made from copies.
templates.needPhotos: Hand over a few photos first, so the album has something in it.
templates.noGit: Git isn't installed on this computer, so the workshop can't borrow a repository. Install git and try again.
templates.notRepo: That folder isn't a git repository, or it has no commits yet. Pick another one.
templates.repairFill: In this code repository, please fix: ...
templates.repairHint: Lend the workshop a code repository. The fixer works on a new branch, and your own branches and anything online stay as they are. You get a review sheet: approve it and the branch stays for you to merge, or turn it down and the branch is deleted.
templates.flowercardFill: Write a card to go with flowers for ..., saying: ...
templates.flowercardHint: The flower shop writes a small card to tuck in with a bouquet: one line, who it is for and who it is from, and a flower drawn on it. Your own words are used as written; if you give none, a line or two is written for you. You get a picture, and a PDF to print.
templates.booklistFill: Make a book list for ..., who wants to read about ...
templates.booklistHint: The bookshop draws up a reading list: eight books unless you ask for more (fifteen at most), in a few groups, each with its author and one line on why. Only books that really exist, and every one is checked. You get a Word document and a PDF.
templates.editHint: Only a copy is edited; your file stays as it is. Text, web pages, Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF, up to 20 MB. A PDF comes back as a Word document.
templates.tidyHint: The staff only see names, sizes and dates. They write you a plan and move nothing.
templates.needSource: Choose the file or folder first.
templates.tooBig: That file is too big (over 20 MB). Try a smaller one.
templates.macros: That file carries macros, which would run when the changed copy is opened, so the shop won't take it. Save it without macros (as .docx, .xlsx or .pptx) and pick it again.

furnish.hint: This room: {scene}. Each room keeps its own colours, and what the shop has gathered stays put.

materials.label: Handed over
materials.hint: Screenshots, spreadsheets, drafts: anything helps. You can also drag files onto this slip or the counter. The staff work from copies; your files stay as they are.
materials.folder: “{name}” is a folder. To sort out a folder, use “Tidy a folder” above.
materials.tooBig: “{name}” is too big (20 MB each, 50 MB in all).
materials.tooMany: Ten files at most; “{name}” will have to wait.
materials.picture: “{name}” is a kind of picture the shop can't open (HEIC or TIFF). Save it as JPG or PNG and hand that over.
materials.busy: The shop is busy with this one. Hand it over when it's done.
materials.drop: Let go to hand it to Wick

lent.pick: Work in a folder I already have…
lent.picked: The staff will change the files in this folder itself. Before a file is first changed, a copy of it is kept as it was, so you can undo the whole commission.
lent.broad: That's too much to hand over. The staff don't work across a whole drive, your home folder, Documents, Desktop or Downloads; pick a smaller folder inside.
lent.tooBig: That folder is too big (over 100 MB). The shop has to be able to keep a copy of everything in it before it can promise an undo. Try a smaller one.
lent.confirmText: The staff will change the files already in this folder without asking about each one. Before any file is first changed, the shop keeps a copy of it as it was.
lent.confirmUndo: If you don't like the result, press “Undo this commission” on the result card: changed files go back as they were, new ones are taken away, and nothing else is touched. Deleting files and running commands still ask you first.
lent.undoAsk: Undoing puts your changed files back as they were and takes away the new ones. What this commission made will be gone.
lent.undone: Undone. The folder is as it was before the work started.
lent.undoPartly: Undone, except for these: {files}. Their folder now leads somewhere outside, and the shop won't write there.
lent.undoFailed: Couldn't undo it; it may have been undone already.

setup.welcomeText: I'm Wick, I run this shop. What should we call you?
setup.welcomeLook: And pick how you look when you drop by:
setup.claudeMissing: Claude Code isn't installed yet. The staff need it to work. It takes about two minutes, once.
setup.claudeStep1: Open PowerShell: press Start, type PowerShell, press Enter.
setup.claudeStep2: Paste this line and press Enter:
setup.claudeStep3: Then come back. The shop notices by itself, no restart needed.
setup.claudeWatching: Waiting for it to finish installing...
setup.claudeInstallHint: Lamplight Nook runs the official installer in the background; no windows open.
setup.claudeInstallFailed: That didn't work. You can install it yourself with the steps below.
setup.claudeOld: Claude Code on this computer is {version}, older than the {tested} the shop has tried. Some jobs may stop partway.
setup.claudeUpdateFailed: That didn't work. You can update it yourself with the steps below: it's the same line as installing.
setup.keyStep1: Sign in to the Anthropic Console, or sign up if you don't have an account.
setup.keyStep2: Add credit under Billing first, at least $5. A key won't work without it.
setup.keyStep3: Under API Keys, create a key, copy it and paste it below.
setup.keyMissing: No API key yet. Paste it below. It's stored encrypted on this computer only.
setup.keyStored: API key saved ({hint}), on this computer only.
setup.keyFromEnv: Using the key in the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable ({hint}).
setup.keySubscription: Developer mode: using the signed-in Claude subscription.
setup.keyUnverified: Can't reach Anthropic right now. Saved anyway; we'll know if it works on the first job.
setup.keyBadFormat: That doesn't look like an API key. It should start with sk-ant-.
setup.keyInvalid: Anthropic says this key doesn't work. Check it was copied in full, or try another.
setup.keyNoStorage: This computer can't store the key encrypted. You can use the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable instead.
setup.laterHint: Not ready? That's fine, come in anyway. Click the counter to watch a trial run.
setup.folderText: Each commission gets its own folder here, with everything that was made.
setup.greetHint: Need something? Write it on the slip at the counter.
setup.readyText: Claude Code and your API key are ready. Write what you need on the commission slip and hand it to Wick.
setup.trialOffer: Want to see how the shop usually works first?
setup.trialEndText: That was a recorded sample: the staff took an "expense tracker" commission. Install Claude Code and add an API key, and you can hand in your own.
setup.lookHint: This is how you'll look when you drop by with a commission.
setup.spendMonth: About {cost} this month. This is Claude Code's estimate. It reports no cost for a stretch stopped partway, so the shop estimates that from what was used. Anthropic's bill is what counts.
setup.modelHint: The slip's More can pick another for one commission. Talking it over with Wick uses Balanced at most.

provider.label: Provider

kinds.compatible: A service with an Anthropic-compatible API
kinds.openai: A service that only speaks the OpenAI format

provider.anthropicHint: The staff use Anthropic's Claude. The key goes in the checks above.
provider.presetDocs: Address and model filled in from {name}'s own setup guide.
provider.keyKept: {hint} is kept; leave empty to keep it
provider.priceHint: The shop cannot know another provider's prices. With them filled in, the caps and the ledger can count; without them, no work starts.
provider.trial: Trial: other makers' models vary in how well they use tools, and the staff may not finish harder commissions.
provider.bedrockKey: Bedrock API key, or "access key ID:secret access key"
provider.credentialsFile: Path of the service account key file
provider.vertexHint: The key file stays where it is; the shop keeps only its path.
provider.openaiText: Claude Code only speaks Anthropic's format. For a service that only speaks OpenAI's, run a gateway such as LiteLLM on this computer first. Once it runs, choose "A service with an Anthropic-compatible API" and give the gateway's address, such as http://localhost:4000.
provider.unverified: Saved, not checked yet. The first commission will tell.

reasons.missing: Something that is needed is still empty.
reasons.shape: The API address is not a web address.
reasons.scheme: The API address must start with https://. Only a gateway on this computer may use http://.
reasons.secret: Keep user names, passwords and anything after a ? out of the address. The key goes below.
reasons.address: Nothing answers at that address, or it is not an API address.
reasons.key: The service says the key does not work.
reasons.model: The service does not know that model.
reasons.storage: This computer cannot encrypt the key, so it was not kept.
reasons.file: That key file is not there.

setup.monthCapHint: At the limit, new work waits. Wick says so before it gets there.

setup.troubleDone: Saved, and selected in its folder for you.
setup.writeText: Or write to us. Lamplight Nook sends nothing itself: it opens the mail program on your computer with the lines below filled in. The rest is yours to write, and sending is up to you.
setup.writeBody: Body: yours to write; the last line names the app version and system, like {footer}
setup.writeDiag: Export the diagnostics file too (drag it into the letter yourself afterwards)
setup.writeOpened: Your mail program is open. What to write, and whether to send it, is up to you.
setup.writeOpenedDiag: Your mail program is open, and the diagnostics file is selected in its folder: drag it into the letter. Sending is up to you.
setup.writeFailed: Your mail program didn't open. You can write to {email} directly.
setup.mailPrompt: (Write what happened here: what you did, and what you saw.)
setup.mailDiag: Diagnostics: {file} (please drag it into this letter)
setup.claudeStoreHint: Three steps below, once. This row turns green by itself when it's done.
setup.claudeStoreUpdate: Three steps below, once (it's the same line as installing). This row turns green by itself when it's done.

setup.legalLine: By opening the shop you agree to the

privacy: # Privacy
Last updated: November 27, 2026
Lamplight Nook collects none of your data: no analytics, no ads, nothing reported in the background. We run no servers and cannot see what happens in your shop.
# What stays on your computer

Your name and settings; your API key, encrypted with the system's own encryption so only you on this computer can unlock it; Wick's notebook (past commissions, the choices you made, where things got stuck); an estimate of what each month cost; records of the last 50 commissions; the last 7 days of the app's log; crash records; your connections and the record of outside actions (a calendar's address is encrypted like the key).

All of this is in the app's data folder (on Windows, %APPDATA%\Lamplight Nook; the Microsoft Store version keeps it in the app's own storage, which Windows removes when you uninstall). You can clear everything the shop remembers from Wick's notebook. Claude Code also keeps its own record of each job, in the .claude folder in your home folder; those belong to Claude Code and stay when you do. If you installed from the setup file, delete that folder after uninstalling to remove everything.
What the staff make goes in the commission folder you chose, and it is yours. Email drafts stay there too: Lamplight Nook never sends them.
# What is sent to Anthropic, or to the provider you chose

The staff work through Claude Code on your computer. Your commissions, anything you add in a meeting, the contents of files the staff read in the commission folder, and web searches are sent to Anthropic through Claude Code with your own API key. If you tick a connection on a commission slip, the files the staff read in the synced folder and the events they read in the calendar are sent to Anthropic the same way. Anthropic's privacy policy and commercial terms apply to that, and the cost goes to your own Anthropic account.
When you save an API key, Lamplight Nook makes one free request to Anthropic to check that it works.
When you talk an order over with Wick, the titles and days of your latest twelve works go along too, so Wick knows which one you mean by “last time”. Not what is in them, nor where they are.

If you choose another provider under Provider in settings (a service with an Anthropic-compatible API, Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex AI), all of the above goes to that provider instead, under its own terms and privacy rules. Each provider's key is stored encrypted on this computer, on its own, and never goes into the log, the diagnostics or the ledger. When you save a compatible service's key, Lamplight Nook sends it the shortest message there is to check the address, key and model, which that provider may charge a tiny amount for.

If you connect a calendar, the calendar's address you gave is used to fetch it straight from this computer. Other than that, Lamplight Nook connects to no servers. When the staff look things up they visit the web pages they find.
# Sharing, postcards and your home network

Sharing a work or sending a postcard saves a file that you pass on yourself; Lamplight Nook uploads nothing for you. A shared work carries the work alone: folder paths, your home folder and anything like a key are wiped from it, and the slip, the staff's notes and the recordings are not in it. A postcard carries only how your shop looks and the name you go by, with no works, commissions, spending or dates.

The home network switch is off by default. When it is on, Lamplight Nook serves a small page on this computer to your home network only, just phones and computers you have paired can connect, and every message is encrypted with the key made when pairing. A paired phone sees what the shop is doing and what it is waiting for you to answer, never your key, folder paths or spending. None of it goes through a server of ours.

One known limit: the page itself reaches the phone over plain HTTP, because a home network has no other way to serve it. Someone else on the same network could change the page on its way, and a changed page could see what that phone sees and do what that device is allowed to do. Turn the switch on only on a network you trust, and off again when you are done.
# Diagnostics

A diagnostics file leaves your computer only when you export it in Settings and send it to us yourself. It holds the app's log and an outline of your computer and settings, with no API key and nothing from your commissions.
# Contact
For questions, use the support contact on Lamplight Nook's Microsoft Store page. If this note changes, it is updated with a new version and the date above changes.
terms: By using Lamplight Nook you agree to these terms.

You are buying a license to use Lamplight Nook yourself on your own devices, not ownership of the software or its assets. Please do not resell, rent out or redistribute Lamplight Nook, or extract its art, sounds, fonts or music to use on their own: they belong to their creators, listed under Third-party licenses.

The staff's work is done by Anthropic's service, which needs your own Anthropic account and API key, used under Anthropic's terms (including their age requirements). Anthropic charges your account for each commission; this is separate from the price of Lamplight Nook.
Spending shown in the shop is Claude Code's estimate; Anthropic's bill is what counts. The per-round limit stops the staff when it is reached as best it can, but the actual cost may go slightly over.

The staff are AI: everything they make is generated by AI, and they make mistakes. Check pages, summaries, edits, tidy-up plans, Office files, pictures, sourced reports and email drafts before you use them, especially before you send them to others or rely on them for a decision. What they make is yours, subject to Anthropic's terms.

The staff work only in the commission folder, and serious steps such as deleting files, running a command they can't vouch for, or writing outside the folder wait for your OK. Even so, keep backups of important files. "Edit a document" only edits a copy, and "Tidy a folder" only writes a plan and moves nothing.

Claude Code and Anthropic's service are provided by Anthropic, not by Lamplight Nook, and we do not control whether they are available or how they behave. The third-party software and assets Lamplight Nook uses, and their licenses, are listed under Third-party licenses.

To the fullest extent the law allows, Lamplight Nook is provided as is, without warranties of any kind; we are not liable for lost data, charges or other indirect losses from using it; and our total liability is limited to what you paid for Lamplight Nook. This does not affect rights that consumer law where you live gives you.
